standard_prerequisites.name: Turing reducibility and E0
standard_prerequisites.statement: Turing reducibility compares the computability strength of sets, and E0 is the equivalence relation of eventual equality of infinite binary sequences.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the relation and the equivalence relation appearing in the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Comeagre and measure-theoretic typicality
standard_prerequisites.statement: The proof reasons about the typical behaviour of sets, where a comeagre or measure-one set of sets has the property or its negation.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the way the contradiction is reached.

standard_prerequisites.name: Saturation-type construction
standard_prerequisites.statement: From the failure of the statement one builds, for each set, a set above it in the given tail, and iterates this to reach the contradiction.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the construction the proof performs.

core_obligations: Assume towards a contradiction that no set has the stated property, so that for every set there is a larger set in its tail that is not equivalent to it under the relation (source lines 565-566).
Use that assumption to build the sequence of sets required by the iterative construction in the source, deriving a contradiction (source lines 566-567).

proof_roadmap.step: Negate the statement and extract the witness for each set.
Iterate the construction to the contradiction.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's unlabelled corollary at source lines 561-563: there is a set of reals such that every set above it in its own tail is equivalent to it under the eventual-equality relation. The author gave it no label, so its position is part of its identity. The proof (source lines 565-567) is a contradiction argument that begins by negating the statement, which supplies for every set a larger set in its tail that is not equivalent, and then runs the iterative construction of the source to reach the contradiction. The statement records only the existence of the set.
